thread:
mira: heads-up — posting follow-up from yesterday's RFC about adding a tiny provenance header + opt-in signature verification for safetensors shards. want to lock on an approach before we start touching loaders.

ben: +1 we need something that avoids a full crypto pass on every warmup. verification is great but can't double our token latency.

sam: can we do a two-tier check? cheap header sanity on hot path, full sig async/parallel after allocation. if sig fails, evict.

olivia: that's basically what i sketched in the doc. cheap header = magic + version + per-shard checksum (crc32) + provenance pointer. full sig = per-bundle signature + optional merkle root.

jordan: question — how do we handle older safetensors that have no header? fallback polyfill?

mira: idea: loader treats absence-of-header as "legacy mode". legacy mode uses existing trust assumptions but emits a continuous audit event. we also send a background verification job that tries to fetch provenance metadata from sidecar manifest store. if manifest proves mismatch, we mark replica unhealthy and trigger rollback.

natalie: i worry about manifest availability in private deployments (on-prem). sidecar store isn't guaranteed. can we store a tiny provenance JSON in S3 adjacent to shard file and still be compliant?

ben: yes — fallbacks should be: 1) in-shard header, 2) adjacent .meta (same bucket, same prefix), 3) central manifest service. loader tries in that order. keep attempts bounded and async.

sam: performance modelling: adding a CRC32 header check is ~50us per shard on our test boxes. full sig/ed25519 is ~800us — too slow for 100ms cold path if we wait. so async verification + eviction on failure is reasonable.

olivia: also propose we include a small "warmup-hint" field in the header: preferred prefetch priority and kv-cache-size estimate. runtime uses that to pick warmup order. avoids separate manifest roundtrip for perf hints.

jordan: what about integrity for multi-shard bundles? attacker could swap shard 3 only. per-shard sigs catch that but operators prefer one canonical bundle signature. merkle root is a sweet spot — cheap aggregated check + per-shard leaf verification if needed.

mira: agreed. plan: header v1 = magic(4) + version(1) + crc32(4) + provenance_pointer(length-prefixed) + warmup_hint(1 byte) + flags(1 byte). v2 adds merkle root and per-shard signature pointer. loader accepts v1 or v2.

natalie: rollout concerns: for Dedicated + Private we need an opt-in runtime flag to enforce verification. default for hosted = verification on, but with async-first-pass to avoid latency spikes. for on-prem we set off by default. docs must be explicit.

ben: PR points: loader read path should be minimal change: detect header ? parse : legacy. if header present, run crc32 sync; queue full verification task to verifier worker pool. verifier publishes audit events (ok/failed + reasons). if failed, runtime triggers evict+fallback and increments health metric.

sam: also add a metric for "header-missing-count" and "async-verify-latency". want to correlate with evictions.

olivia: implementation note — don't allocate GPU buffers before minimal header check. allocate after crc32. reduces wasted mem pressure when loading bad blobs.

mira: tentative owner list: ben + olivia run loader changes; sam + jordan implement verifier service + merkle tools; natalie coordinates rollout + docs. i'll draft a short RFC addendum with v1 header bytes and a compatibility matrix.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: verifier-service -> canary (eng-ml) at 2026-04-02T18:00Z.

ben: follow-ups: i'll open the loader PR and include microbench numbers for crc32/sig async. expect draft by EOD Fri.

mira: thanks — if anyone objects to the plan reply here. otherwise i'll publish addendum and create the tracker ticket. :thumbsup:
